tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

/** What the builder may save now. */
export const offeredQueriesSchema = (scalable: ScalableArtifactAccess) => queriesSchema(offeredSources(scalable));
export type ArtifactQuery = z.infer<typeof artifactQueriesSchema>[number];

const shift = (date: string, days: number) => new Date(Date.parse(`${date}T00:00:00Z`) + days * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
function monthStart(date: string, offset = 0) {
  const at = new Date(`${date.slice(0, 7)}-01T00:00:00Z`);
  at.setUTCMonth(at.getUTCMonth() + offset);
  return at.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
}
const monthEnd = (date: string, offset = 0) => shift(monthStart(date, offset + 1), -1);
const yearStart = (date: string, offset = 0) => `${Number(date.slice(0, 4)) + offset}-01-01`;
const weekStart = (date: string) => shift(date, -((new Date(`${date}T00:00:00Z`).getUTCDay() + 6) % 7));

/** Ranges and values of a card's params, resolved for this view. */
export type ResolvedParams = { values: Record<string, string>; ranges: Record<string, { from: string; to: string }> };

/**
 * Saved inputs keep their meaning over time: a date written as a token resolves against today in the
 * workspace's timezone, so "this month" stays the calendar month. Literal dates stay fixed.
 *   @today  @days_ago:N  @week_start  @month_start[:±N]  @month_end[:±N]  @year_start[:±N]  @year_end[:±N]
 *   @param:name (a choice param's value)  @param:name.from  @param:name.to (a month or period param's range)
 */
export function resolveToken(value: string, today: string, params: ResolvedParams = { values: {}, ranges: {} }): string {
  const param = /^@param:([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,39})(?:\.(from|to))?$/.exec(value);
  if (param) {
    const [, name, end] = param;
    const resolved = end ? params.ranges[name]?.[end as "from" | "to"] : params.values[name];
    if (resolved === undefined) throw new Error(`Unknown param ${value}`);
    return resolved;
  }
  const token = /^@(today|days_ago|week_start|month_start|month_end|year_start|year_end)(?::(-?\d{1,4}))?$/.exec(value);
  if (!token) return value;
  const n = Number(token[2] ?? 0);
  switch (token[1]) {
    case "today": return shift(today, n);
    case "days_ago": return shift(today, -n);
    case "week_start": return shift(weekStart(today), n * 7);
    case "month_start": return monthStart(today, n);
    case "month_end": return monthEnd(today, n);
    case "year_start": return yearStart(today, n);
    default: return `${Number(today.slice(0, 4)) + n}-12-31`;
  }
}

## 5. Second research round (2026-11-15): what is already taken, what is open

Checked each idea from section 3 against the literature. Most of them have close neighbours:

| Idea | Already published | Still open |
|---|---|---|
| Listen with knowledge of own speech | Textual Echo Cancellation (Google 2020, arXiv 2008.06006) uses the TTS text as echo reference; implicit AEC (Amazon, arXiv 2111.10639) feeds the reference into the classifier; Self-Listening (arXiv 2609.05592); PACE | Doing it in a sub-MB head on a 17 MB recogniser on CPU |
| Tiny turn/state head on recogniser features | Voice-Light adapter (183K weights, failed), SoulX-Duplug (0.6B LLM, GPU, user audio only), FSM tapes (arXiv 2609.03321) | Small and CPU, with the playback as input |
| Start work before the sentence ends | Personalized Predictive ASR (Amazon, Interspeech 2023, arXiv 2305.13794) predicts the full utterance and prefetches; Speculative Speech Recognition (arXiv 2407.04641); Endpoint Anticipation (arXiv 2606.13450, 505 ms saved, 28% extra compute); Voice-Light | Tools with read/write safety |
| Local fast path learned from a big model | Distil Labs banking voice assistant (0.35-0.6B tool-calling model distilled offline, about 40 ms); Agentic Plan Caching (NeurIPS 2025); AgenticCache (MLSys 2026, background validator); Google patent on distilling from observed query patterns | Learning online from the owner's own calls with background checking |
| Think between calls | Sleep-time Compute (arXiv 2504.13171); "Don't Wait to Reply" (arXiv 2607.03093) | Voice, personal data, validity tied to data version |
| Per-user turn-taking | Bandit endpointing (arXiv 2303.13407), speaker-embedding endpointing (SLT 2021) | On-device learning from the owner's interruptions |

const shift = (date: string, days: number) => new Date(Date.parse(`${date}T00:00:00Z`) + days * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
function monthStart(date: string, offset = 0) {
  const at = new Date(`${date.slice(0, 7)}-01T00:00:00Z`);
  at.setUTCMonth(at.getUTCMonth() + offset);
  return at.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
}
const monthEnd = (date: string, offset = 0) => shift(monthStart(date, offset + 1), -1);
const yearStart = (date: string, offset = 0) => `${Number(date.slice(0, 4)) + offset}-01-01`;
const weekStart = (date: string) => shift(date, -((new Date(`${date}T00:00:00Z`).getUTCDay() + 6) % 7));

/** Ranges and values of a card's params, resolved for this view. */
export type ResolvedParams = { values: Record<string, string>; ranges: Record<string, { from: string; to: string }> };

/**
 * Saved inputs keep their meaning over time: a date written as a token resolves against today in the
 * workspace's timezone, so "this month" stays the calendar month. Literal dates stay fixed.
 *   @today  @days_ago:N  @week_start  @month_start[:±N]  @month_end[:±N]  @year_start[:±N]  @year_end[:±N]
 *   @param:name (a choice param's value)  @param:name.from  @param:name.to (a month or period param's range)
 */
export function resolveToken(value: string, today: string, params: ResolvedParams = { values: {}, ranges: {} }): string {
  const param = /^@param:([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,39})(?:\.(from|to))?$/.exec(value);
  if (param) {
    const [, name, end] = param;
    const resolved = end ? params.ranges[name]?.[end as "from" | "to"] : params.values[name];
    if (resolved === undefined) throw new Error(`Unknown param ${value}`);
    return resolved;
  }
  const token = /^@(today|days_ago|week_start|month_start|month_end|year_start|year_end)(?::(-?\d{1,4}))?$/.exec(value);
  if (!token) return value;
  const n = Number(token[2] ?? 0);
  switch (token[1]) {
    case "today": return shift(today, n);
    case "days_ago": return shift(today, -n);
    case "week_start": return shift(weekStart(today), n * 7);
    case "month_start": return monthStart(today, n);
    case "month_end": return monthEnd(today, n);
    case "year_start": return yearStart(today, n);
    default: return `${Number(today.slice(0, 4)) + n}-12-31`;
  }
}

input.description: Write blind editor test set
input.prompt:
You are writing a blind test set for a voice assistant in a personal-finance app. Do NOT read any code in the repository (the test must be blind to the implementation). Only write one file and reply with a two-line summary.

Write exactly 300 lines of JSONL to:
C:\Users\mgsuk\.t3\worktrees\Moneo\t3-846dd64c-f0b28664becb1320\research\voice-duplex\experiments\expE\editor_cases.jsonl
(create the folder). Write the file with UTF-8 encoding. Generate it however you like (by hand or with a small script you write in your scratch space), but every line must be valid JSON and the utterances must be varied and natural, like real people talking on a phone call to their finance app: disfluencies ("um", "uh"), restarts, casual wording, different sentence shapes. Write the text the way a speech recogniser would output it: mostly lowercase, little or no punctuation, numbers sometimes as words ("thirty days") and sometimes digits ("30 days"). English only.

## What each line is
{"id":"e001","kind":"...","turns":["first thing the owner says","second thing", ...],"gold":{...} or null}

`turns` are the owner's utterances in one call, in order. `gold` is the question card AFTER the last turn, or null when the last turn asks something the card cannot express (then the app hands over to a big chat model).

## The card
{"metric":"spending"|"income"|"net"|"count","categories":[...],"merchants":[...],"accounts":[...],"period":{"from":"YYYY-MM-DD","to":"YYYY-MM-DD"},"comparison":{"from":..,"to":..}|null,"groupBy":"category"|"merchant"|"account"|"month"|null}

- metric: spending (what was spent/paid/cost), income (earned/made/received), net (income minus spending, "did I save", "net", "cash flow"), count (how many transactions/times/purchases).
- categories/merchants/accounts: exact names from the owner's lists below (use the exact spelling from the list in gold). Several names of one kind mean "any of these".
- groupBy: set when the owner asks for a breakdown or a ranking ("by category", "which merchant", "where did my money go" = category, "per month").
- Defaults when not said: metric spending, no filters, period = this calendar month, comparison null, groupBy null.

## The owner's names (the only ones that exist)
Categories: Groceries, Restaurants, Rent, Transport, Travel, Subscriptions, Health, Shopping, Utilities, Salary, Entertainment, Coffee
Merchants: Rewe, Lidl, Amazon, Netflix, Spotify, Uber, Deutsche Bahn, Ikea, Apple, Shell
Accounts: N26, Revolut, Sparkasse Giro, Amex, Cash
People may say singular/plural variants of these names ("grocery", "restaurant", "subscription"); do NOT use synonyms that are not the name (no "food" for Groceries).

## Dates. Today is Sunday 2026-11-15.
- today = 2026-11-15..2026-11-15; yesterday = 2026-11-14.
- this week = Monday to Sunday containing today: 2026-11-09..2026-11-15. last week = 2026-11-02..2026-11-08.
- this month = 2026-11-01..2026-11-30 (the whole calendar month). last month = 2026-10-01..2026-10-31.
- this year = 2026-01-01..2026-12-31. last year = 2025-01-01..2025-12-31. "in 2024" = that calendar year.
- A month name without a year = the latest such month that has started ("in March" = 2026-03-01..2026-03-31, "in December" = 2025-12-01..2025-12-31, "in November" = 2026-11). "last October" = latest October that has ended (2026-10). "October 2025" = that month.
- "the last/past N days" = N days ending today inclusive ("last 30 days" = 2026-10-17..2026-11-15). "last N weeks" = 7N days ending today. "the last/past N months" and "the past month" = from the day after the same date N months ago to today ("last 3 months" = 2026-08-16..2026-11-15). "the past year" = 2025-11-16..2026-11-15.
- comparison: "compared to / versus / than <period>" sets comparison to that period. "compared to the month before" or a bare "how does that compare" = the period right before the main period (whole months stay whole months; other ranges keep their length).

## How turns combine
- A full new question that has its own verb of money (spend, pay, cost, earn, make, how many...) and does not open with "and", "what about", "how about", "also", "same for", "or", "but", or a correction word, starts a NEW card from the defaults.
- A short follow-up ("and last month", "what about restaurants", "same for Amex") keeps everything from the previous card and changes only what it mentions; a name it mentions REPLACES the previous names of that kind.
- A correction, inside one turn or as a new short turn ("no, last month", "sorry I meant restaurants", "not groceries, restaurants", "actually make that amazon"), replaces the corrected thing. Last one said wins.
- Without a correction word, two names of one kind in the same turn are both kept ("groceries and restaurants").
- In a follow-up that switches between spending and income without repeating a category or merchant, the categories and merchants are dropped (accounts and period stay).

## Kinds and how many (300 total)
- "plain" 60: one turn, one clear question (mix metrics, filters, periods; at least 15 with two filters).
- "self-correction" 60: ONE turn in which the owner changes their mind mid-sentence about the period, a name, the metric, or the comparison period.
- "follow-up" 50: 2 or 3 turns; later turns are short follow-ups.
- "interruption" 40: 2 turns; the second is a short correction spoken over the assistant's answer ("no last month", "wait i said rewe not lidl", "not this year last year").
- "compare" 30: one turn with a comparison.

I'm setting up an eval script that splits the cases into dev (odd ids) and held-out test (even ids), so I can iterate only on dev and still report both. The script will load the cases and vocab, run editCard across turns, and check whether the final turn is answerable.

I'm checking how to score the gold cases: a null gold counts as correct only when the turn isn't answerable, and a card gold counts as correct only when it's answerable and the card matches. I'm also going to measure unsafe prefixes on the last turn, meaning word prefixes that are answerable but differ from the final card.

I'm looking at the first-pass dev results: 76% exact, 3% wrong, 21% handed off, with no false accepts on out-of-scope queries, so it's a solid baseline to iterate from. Now I'm sorting the failures into classes, starting with "quick question" inputs where the leftover word "question" is hurting detection, and a follow-up like "sorry last month" that ends up with categories dropped because the base from the first turn is null.

Now I'm working through the remaining failure class: STT renders names like "N26" as "n twenty six," so entity matching misses them. My plan is to normalise number words to digits and split letter-digit boundaries on both sides before matching, so both forms reduce to the same canonical string.

Next I'm widening the matching so "n twenty six" and "N26" meet in the same canonical form, which means folding number words into digits and splitting letter-digit boundaries on both sides. I'm also planning to treat "card" or "account" as filler right after an account name, and to add "into", "back", "anything", and "saving" to the fillers and the net cue.

I'm also checking the follow-up case: "and how much did I earn" opens with "and," which the gold labels as a follow-up that keeps the accounts and period but drops categories and merchants, yet our `follows` check on the first non-pause token may be treating it as a fresh question.

Now I'm checking the follow-up handling: the leftover "card" on the first turn left the base null, so the "and how much did I earn" follow-up started from nothing, and fixing the card filler should resolve that. I'm also going through the remaining cases, like the "thirty days before" period phrase and whether "most" can be allowed as a filler when a grouping cue is already present.

I'm widening the early-card detection: prefixes like "how much did I spend" are already answerable for this month before the category is named, and that's where most of the 42% early-card difference comes from. The wrong-number risk if someone says it all at once is the reason I'm keeping the ranking words like "most" and "break down" as leftovers to filter out only when a grouping cue is present.

Now I'm writing a helper that turns number words into digits and separates letters from digits, so "n twenty six" and "N26" reduce to the same form before matching.

Now I'm writing the spoken-form helper: number words become digits and letters split from digits, so "N26" and "n twenty six" both reduce to "n 26". The same key gets applied to entity names and to the utterance slice, which is how the matcher will line them up.

Now I'm writing the continuation of the token-matching helper, with the canonical key built from the entity names and utterance slices, and working out how far the longest-match window needs to reach.

Now I'm adding a flag that tracks whether the previous matched token was an account entity, so a following "card" or "account" can be skipped as filler. I'm also adding "question", "into", "back", "anything", "end", "go", and "saving" to the fillers and net cue, and starting to write a period reader that handles "N units before".

Now I'm adding the period reader case: a count followed by a unit and "before", optionally "that", maps to the period just before the current one. I'm also planning to filter out ranking words like "most" and "break down" at the end, but only when a grouping cue is already set.

content.thinking:
I'm sorting out the held-out failure cases, starting with the "compare X this month to in august" pattern. The word "compare" comes before both time periods, so I need to handle two periods there: the first one fills the period slot and the second fills the comparison slot.

I'm adding handling for a bare "compare" cue: the first period fills the period slot and the next one fills the comparison slot, with a correction then overwriting the comparison. I'm also noting that "compare to" counts as a two-word cue rather than a bare verb, and that "hang on" works as a correction marker.

I'm adding a few more filler words for the count cues, like "buy", "order", and "take", and handling phrase variants for "where did my money go". I'm also working out that "monthly breakdown" shouldn't override a grouping that was already set explicitly in the same utterance.

I'm weighing a case where a balance question like "how much money do I have in revolut" could be wrongly answered as spending, since "have" is currently a filler word and nothing in it names a metric. My plan is to only accept a turn as answerable when the user's own words establish a metric, a grouping, or a comparison, and to hand off balance-style questions instead.

I'm working out a rule for when a "how much" question with no metric cue should be handed off instead of answered as spending, since a balance question like "how much money is in my sparkasse giro" would otherwise get misread. Follow-up leads such as "how about" or "what about" still need to carry through as answerable, and I'm checking that the rule doesn't catch them.

I'm working through the "how much" case now: a question with no metric cue, like a balance question, should be handed off rather than answered as spending. I'm considering a rule that flags that kind of "how much" turn as unexplained unless it's a follow-up with a lead word, and I'm checking whether follow-up questions without a lead would get caught by mistake.

I'm settling on the fix for the held-out cases, though the fixed test half means I can't treat the result as a clean final number. I'll build a fresh set written in a different style and score it once, without tuning afterward.

The first-run v2 results look like 88% exact, 3% wrong, and 10% handed off, with all 40 out-of-scope cases correctly handed off and no false accepts. On the audit's E4 bar, the self-correction slice only reaches 70% on the first run, so that part falls short even though the overall number is 88%.

I'm weighing a narrower guard for "how much" questions with no metric cue: send them to handoff only when they name just an account, and treat them as spending when a merchant is named, since "uber this week how much" has only one sensible reading. That still leaves "how much salary did I get," which would wrongly land on spending, so I'm considering adding income cues like "get" and "got" while watching that "get" doesn't pull in filler uses.

I'm planning to treat "get me" and "give me" as polite filler so that "get" doesn't push "how much" questions toward income, and then I'll add "get" and "got" as income cues. Next I want to relax the guard so it only sends a "how much" question to handoff when it names accounts without a metric, and I'll check the restaurants and "uber not uber" cases that hit that guard. For the "make it sixty days" correction, I'm considering letting a bare number plus unit after a correction count as a rolling period.

I'm thinking about widening the bare-number rule so that "30 days" counts as a rolling period, since in this domain it rarely means anything else. The "in 30 days" future phrasing is already handed off by the "will" check, so that risk is covered. I'm also looking at the count-versus-spending mix-up in the ikea case, where a correction should let the later metric cue win.

I'm going to let "would" count as a polite filler again, with "would like", "i would", and "id like" as bigrams so they drop out of the leftover check. Counting nouns like orders, rides, and visits can also be treated as filler when the metric is a count, so "how many amazon orders" stops leaving stray words behind.

I'm now thinking through the remaining spending-query cases: "how much would I spend if" leaves a stray "if", so I'm considering a "i would" bigram as filler. I'd also treat "both" as filler for the Lidl and Rewe groceries case and let the last mentioned month win for the salary query, with "get" counting as an income cue there.

I'm now fixing the "make that" case: the correction phrase is two words, but the single-word metric "make" gets matched first as an income cue. So I'll check for the two-word correction before adding the metric option, and skip the metric when it's there.

I'm checking the "how many times ... at lidl ... how much ... there" case: "shop" is only a groupBy word after "by", so it leaks into the leftover words in the first turn and sends the base to handoff. Adding "shop" and "shopped" as fillers, alongside "there," should let the second turn resolve to spending.

I'm now working out a follow-up problem: if the previous turn was handed off, a correction that leans on it shouldn't be answered against an empty base. I'm thinking about having the edit step report whether the utterance depends on the prior turn, so the caller can hand off in that case too.

Since the earlier turn was handed off, I'm weighing whether a follow-up like "and last month?" should still be answered from the card as it stood before that turn, or handed off instead, since the gold rule keeps the card unchanged but the follow-up's meaning is ambiguous without the handed-off context. I'm leaning toward handing it off to stay safe.

I'm planning to make a follow-up that leans on a handed-off turn hand off as well, so it doesn't get answered against a missing base. A fresh elliptical question at the start of a call can still be answered, since nothing earlier is being built on. I'll also check the "get last month" correction case, where the first turn is handed off by the guard, and the count-noun cases like "number of uber rides in october" and "how many amazon orders this year."

I'm looking at "purchases" as a spending word and weighing whether to add it to the spending cues. I'm also planning a narrower guard: send a question to handoff only when it names accounts with no category or merchant and no metric cue, instead of keying on "how much" alone.

I'm settling on the final rules now: the guard will send accounts-only questions with no metric to handoff, and I'll apply the bundle of fixes. After this pass I'll freeze the rules, treat the first-run v2 result (88/3/10) as the reported number, and leave further tuning to the learned tagger.

content.thinking:
The investigate() call is slow, around 225 ms for 20k rows, because it sorts and SHA-256 hashes the JSON of every row on each call just to build the evidence ID. One option is to pre-filter the rows by period before calling it, so the hashing runs over fewer rows.

I'm weighing a caller-side date prefilter so investigate() only hashes rows inside the requested period or comparison, which should cut the cost to about 6 ms for a month and 75 ms for a year. Sorting by date and binary searching would still hash everything, and adding an option to skip the evidence hash would touch verified core code, so I'm leaning toward the prefilter. I also want to cap the month breakdown at 6 groups, falling back to the agent beyond that since 11 or 12 months is too long to speak.

const marker='## 6. Sources';
const add=`## 7. Audit of the live-query plan (2026-11-15, one Fable agent, read the codebase)

Verdict: **right direction, wrong plan as written.** Build it as a typed fast path with the chat agent as fallback, not as a new query language.

What the audit corrected:

| Claim in section 5 | Audit finding |
|---|---|
| First incremental edit parsing from streaming speech | Not new: Zhou et al. ACL 2022 (prefix-to-program parsing), TERTiUS (arXiv 2307.04008), Disfl-QA |
| Typed query as dialogue state | Not new: SMCalFlow, Trummer's CiceroDB / voice OLAP, Evizeon (VAST 2017) |
| Speech as a view of data, re-bound mid-sentence | Not new as an idea: Buschmeier et al. SIGDIAL 2012 (incremental generation that adapts while speaking) |
| Live number guard: nothing found | Wrong. A patent covers checking synthesised speech before playback |
| We need a query language | Wrong. \`investigationSchema\` + \`investigate()\` + \`/money/investigations?query=\` already are one |

The claim that survives: **a full-duplex cascade whose dialogue state is an executable typed query, re-evaluated on every recogniser increment including overlapped speech, with in-turn re-binding of data-grounded answers, on a laptop CPU**, scored on FDB-v3 self-correction, EchoChain (arXiv 2604.16456) and Duplex Cue.

Risks named: the headline (edit while the assistant speaks) rests on the weakest measured part (ears: about 1 s to stop, 6/24 missed). Coverage is unmeasured (audit's guess: 45-60% of reads, 30-45% of all delegated requests).

Codebase constraints to respect: route handlers cannot upgrade WebSockets and the proxy buffers bodies (so a sidecar port or in-browser models); everything binds to 127.0.0.1; the desktop app ships no Python (ONNX or native runtimes only); repo is MIT, so Pocket TTS ships and Woof is an optional download, never training audio; today's call speaks English and German, so GPT-Live stays selectable; record audio only against \`moneo-qa\`; \`investigate()\` caveats (one total per currency, null on missing FX, partial coverage) must be spoken; fast answers must be saved to the conversation; the in-memory snapshot is stale after a card is accepted or \`sourceRevision\` changes.

Four tests that can kill the idea early:

| Test | What | Pass bar | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 coverage | Replay real past call requests through the fast path | answers 50%+ of reads and 35%+ of all; same answer as the agent 98%+ | the owner's own data, run by the owner |
| E2 ears | Real microphone, 3+ speakers, 40 corrections + 40 backchannels over playback | 90% of interruptions caught within 400 ms; slot words right 85%+; false stops 10% or less | \`moneo-qa\`, real devices |
| E3 preference | Clips: re-bind mid-sentence vs stop and restart | listeners prefer re-bind | about 12 listeners |
| E4 editor | Rule editor on streamed word sequences | final card exact 80%+ on self-corrections; wrong-number exposure 5% or less | done first, see section 8 |

## 8. First build slice and E4 (2026-11-15)

Code (in \`lib/ai/\`, pure functions, no I/O, 14 unit tests):

| File | Job |
|---|---|
| \`voice-query.ts\` | The question card (metric, categories, merchants, accounts, period, comparison, breakdown), spoken periods resolved to exact dates, and the card as input for the existing \`investigate()\` |
| \`voice-query-editor.ts\` | \`editCard(base, words so far)\`: re-run on every new word. Last mention wins, short follow-ups edit the previous card, full questions start a new one. Returns \`leftover\`: every word it could not explain. Non-empty leftover means "hand to the chat model" |
| \`voice-say.ts\` | Exact money in words (bigint, never rounds), the answer as ordered pieces with the number last, and \`rebind()\`: where speech resumes after the card changed |
| \`voice-fast-answer.ts\` | \`fastAnswer()\`: words -> card -> \`investigate()\` on rows in memory -> sentence, or null |

E4, editor accuracy. Test sets written by a separate agent that never saw the rules (\`experiments/expE\`): set 1 has 300 cases (script-assisted, repetitive phrasing), set 2 has 200 hand-written cases in 20 speaking styles. Each case is 1-3 turns with a gold card, or "must hand off".

| Run | Exact | Wrong answer | Handed off | Out-of-scope refused |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Set 1 odd half, first try | 76% | 3% | 21% | 20/20 |
| Set 1 even half, first try after tuning on the odd half | 82% | 9% | 9% | 18/20 |
| **Set 2, first try after tuning on set 1 (the honest number)** | **88%** | **3%** | **10%** | **40/40** |
| Set 2 self-corrections only, first try | 70% | 3% | 28% | - |
| All sets after tuning on them | 99-100% | 0% | 0-1% | 80/80 |

Reading: rules reach the bar only after seeing the data, so the honest state is 88% exact, 3% wrong. The 80% self-correction bar was missed on first try (70%). Wrong answers came from three causes, all now fixed and all worth keeping as rules: a follow-up after a handed-off turn, a question with no money verb about an account ("how much is in Revolut" is a balance), and words that are both a verb and a correction ("make that"). A new blind set is needed before quoting a final number, and the learned tagger (later step) has to beat 88/3.

Early cards: in 49-60% of partial transcripts the card is complete but not yet the final one ("how much did I spend" before "on groceries"). So nothing may be spoken the moment a card looks complete; the gate (pause detection) and number-last speech are required, not optional.

Speed: one edit 0.1 ms. Whole fast path (edit + query + sentence): 2,000 rows 4 ms median / 9 ms p95; 20,000 rows 33 / 95 ms; 100,000 rows 176 / 505 ms. \`investigate()\` fingerprints every row it is given (sort + SHA-256), which was 225 ms at 20,000 rows until the fast path pre-filtered rows by date.

Not covered yet, by design (all go to the chat model): balances, net worth, budgets, recurring, forecasts, averages, exclusions, amount conditions, single transactions, tags, synonyms ("food" for Groceries), every write.

## 9. Plan after the audit

See \`plan.html\` (rebuilt) for the diagrams. Order:

| Step | Build | Gate (loop until it passes) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Card, editor rules, speech, fast answer (done) | E4: 80%+ exact on a fresh blind set, 2% or less wrong, 100% of out-of-scope refused |
| 2 | Fast path inside today's GPT-Live call, text only: answered turns skip \`/api/chat\`, are saved to the conversation, and fall back on null | E1 coverage on the owner's history; same answer as the agent 98%+; p95 under 150 ms |
| 3 | More card kinds: balances, net worth, recurring, budget left | E1 again: coverage up, wrong answers still 2% or less |
| 4 | Real-microphone harness on \`moneo-qa\` and the ears (echo cancelling + a model that also hears the playback) | E2 |
| 5 | Local engine behind a setting: Whistle + turn head in, Pocket TTS / Woof out, same event names as today | First sound under 500 ms median; numbers spoken right 99%+ |
| 6 | Re-bindable speech and the number guard (digit sequence of what was synthesised vs the card) | E3; wrong number reaching the speaker under 1% |
| 7 | Learned editor: distil a small tagger from the rules plus chat-model labels; rules stay as the safety net | Beats rules on a fresh blind set |
| 8 | Scoring: GPT-Live measured on the same script, FDB-v3 self-correction, EchoChain, Duplex Cue; write-up | Better than GPT-Live on self-correction and wrong-number rate |

`;
if(!s.includes(marker)) throw new Error('marker');
s=s.replace(marker, add+'## 10. Sources');
s+=`- Audit additions: Zhou et al. ACL 2022 (online semantic parsing for latency reduction); TERTiUS https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.04008 ; EchoChain https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16456 ; Buschmeier, Baumann, Dosch, Kopp, Schlangen, SIGDIAL 2012 ; Trummer, CiceroDB ; Evizeon (IEEE VAST 2017) ; Disfl-QA
`;
fs.writeFileSync(p,s);
EOF
node "$TEMP/log.cjs" && grep -n "^## " research/voice-duplex/LOG.md && sed -n 1,40p research/voice-duplex/plan.html

## 7. Audit of the live-query plan (2026-11-15, one Fable agent, read the codebase)

Verdict: **right direction, wrong plan as written.** Build it as a typed fast path with the chat agent as fallback, not as a new query language.

What the audit corrected:

| Claim in section 5 | Audit finding |
|---|---|
| First incremental edit parsing from streaming speech | Not new: Zhou et al. ACL 2022 (prefix-to-program parsing), TERTiUS (arXiv 2307.04008), Disfl-QA |
| Typed query as dialogue state | Not new: SMCalFlow, Trummer's CiceroDB / voice OLAP, Evizeon (VAST 2017) |
| Speech as a view of data, re-bound mid-sentence | Not new as an idea: Buschmeier et al. SIGDIAL 2012 (incremental generation that adapts while speaking) |
| Live number guard: nothing found | Wrong. A patent covers checking synthesised speech before playback |
| We need a query language | Wrong. `investigationSchema` + `investigate()` + `/money/investigations?query=` already are one |

The claim that survives: **a full-duplex cascade whose dialogue state is an executable typed query, re-evaluated on every recogniser increment including overlapped speech, with in-turn re-binding of data-grounded answers, on a laptop CPU**, scored on FDB-v3 self-correction, EchoChain (arXiv 2604.16456) and Duplex Cue.

Risks named: the headline (edit while the assistant speaks) rests on the weakest measured part (ears: about 1 s to stop, 6/24 missed). Coverage is unmeasured (audit's guess: 45-60% of reads, 30-45% of all delegated requests).

Codebase constraints to respect: route handlers cannot upgrade WebSockets and the proxy buffers bodies (so a sidecar port or in-browser models); everything binds to 127.0.0.1; the desktop app ships no Python (ONNX or native runtimes only); the repo is MIT, so Pocket TTS ships and Woof is an optional download, never training audio; today's call speaks English and German, so GPT-Live stays selectable; record audio only against `moneo-qa`; `investigate()` caveats (one total per currency, null on missing FX, partial coverage) must be spoken; fast answers must be saved to the conversation; the in-memory snapshot is stale after a card is accepted or `sourceRevision` changes.

Four tests that can kill the idea early:

| Test | What | Pass bar | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 coverage | Replay real past call requests through the fast path | answers 50%+ of reads and 35%+ of all; same answer as the agent 98%+ | the owner's own data, run by the owner |
| E2 ears | Real microphone, 3+ speakers, 40 corrections + 40 backchannels over playback | 90% of interruptions caught within 400 ms; slot words right 85%+; false stops 10% or less | `moneo-qa`, real devices |
| E3 preference | Clips: re-bind mid-sentence vs stop and restart | listeners prefer re-bind | about 12 listeners |
| E4 editor | Rule editor on streamed word sequences | final card exact 80%+ on self-corrections; wrong-number exposure 5% or less | done first, see section 8 |

## 8. First build slice and E4 (2026-11-15)

Code (in `lib/ai/`, pure functions, no I/O, 14 unit tests):

| File | Job |
|---|---|
| `voice-query.ts` | The question card (metric, categories, merchants, accounts, period, comparison, breakdown), spoken periods resolved to exact dates, and the card as input for the existing `investigate()` |
| `voice-query-editor.ts` | `editCard(base, words so far)`: re-run on every new word. Last mention wins, short follow-ups edit the previous card, full questions start a new one. Returns `leftover`: every word it could not explain. Non-empty leftover means "hand to the chat model" |
| `voice-say.ts` | Exact money in words (bigint, never rounds), the answer as ordered pieces with the number last, and `rebind()`: where speech resumes after the card changed |
| `voice-fast-answer.ts` | `fastAnswer()`: words -> card -> `investigate()` on rows in memory -> sentence, or null |

E4, editor accuracy. Test sets were written by a separate agent that never saw the rules (`experiments/expE`): set 1 has 300 cases (script-assisted, repetitive phrasing), set 2 has 200 hand-written cases in 20 speaking styles. Each case is 1-3 turns with a gold card, or "must hand off".

| Run | Exact | Wrong answer | Handed off | Out-of-scope refused |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Set 1 odd half, first try | 76% | 3% | 21% | 20/20 |
| Set 1 even half, first try after tuning on the odd half | 82% | 9% | 9% | 18/20 |
| **Set 2, first try after tuning on set 1 (the honest number)** | **88%** | **3%** | **10%** | **40/40** |
| Set 2 self-corrections only, first try | 70% | 3% | 28% | - |
| All sets after tuning on them | 99-100% | 0% | 0-1% | 80/80 |

Reading: rules reach the bar only after seeing the data, so the honest state is 88% exact, 3% wrong. The 80% self-correction bar was missed on the first try (70%). Wrong answers came from three causes, all now fixed and all worth keeping as rules: a follow-up after a handed-off turn, a question with no money verb about an account ("how much is in Revolut" is a balance), and words that are both a verb and a correction ("make that"). A new blind set is needed before quoting a final number, and the learned tagger (later step) has to beat 88/3.

Early cards: in 49-60% of partial transcripts the card is complete but not yet the final one ("how much did I spend" before "on groceries"). So nothing may be spoken the moment a card looks complete; the gate (pause detection) and number-last speech are required, not optional. True wrong-number exposure needs word timings from audio and is not measured yet.

Speed: one edit 0.1 ms. Whole fast path (edit + query + sentence) on a synthetic ledger: 2,000 rows 4 ms median / 9 ms p95; 20,000 rows 33 / 95 ms; 100,000 rows 176 / 505 ms. `investigate()` fingerprints every row it is given (sort + SHA-256), which cost 225 ms at 20,000 rows until the fast path pre-filtered rows by date.

Not covered yet, by design (all go to the chat model): balances, net worth, budgets, recurring, forecasts, averages, exclusions, amount conditions, single transactions, tags, synonyms ("food" for Groceries), every write.

## 9. Plan after the audit

See `plan.html` (rebuilt) for the diagrams. Order:

| Step | Build | Gate (loop until it passes) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Card, editor rules, speech, fast answer (done) | E4: 80%+ exact on a fresh blind set, 2% or less wrong, 100% of out-of-scope refused |
| 2 | Fast path inside today's GPT-Live call, text only: answered turns skip `/api/chat`, are saved to the conversation, and fall back on null | E1 coverage on the owner's history; same answer as the agent 98%+; p95 under 150 ms |
| 3 | More card kinds: balances, net worth, recurring, budget left | E1 again: coverage up, wrong answers still 2% or less |
| 4 | Real-microphone harness on `moneo-qa` and the ears (echo cancelling + a model that also hears the playback) | E2 |
| 5 | Local engine behind a setting: Whistle + turn head in, Pocket TTS / Woof out, same event names as today | First sound under 500 ms median; numbers spoken right 99%+ |
| 6 | Re-bindable speech and the number guard (digit sequence of what was synthesised vs the card) | E3; wrong number reaching the speaker under 1% |
| 7 | Learned editor: distil a small tagger from the rules plus chat-model labels; rules stay as the safety net | Beats rules on a fresh blind set |
| 8 | Scoring: GPT-Live measured on the same script, FDB-v3 self-correction, EchoChain, Duplex Cue; write-up | Better than GPT-Live on self-correction and wrong-number rate |

| `voice-say.ts` | Exact money in words (bigint, never rounds), the answer as ordered pieces with the number last, and `rebind()`: where speech resumes after the card changed |
| `voice-fast-answer.ts` | `fastAnswer()`: words -> card -> `investigate()` on rows in memory -> sentence, or null |

E4, editor accuracy. Test sets were written by a separate agent that never saw the rules (`experiments/expE`): set 1 has 300 cases (script-assisted, repetitive phrasing), set 2 has 200 hand-written cases in 20 speaking styles. Each case is 1-3 turns with a gold card, or "must hand off".

| Run | Exact | Wrong answer | Handed off | Out-of-scope refused |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Set 1 odd half, first try | 76% | 3% | 21% | 20/20 |
| Set 1 even half, first try after tuning on the odd half | 82% | 9% | 9% | 18/20 |
| **Set 2, first try after tuning on set 1 (the honest number)** | **88%** | **3%** | **10%** | **40/40** |
| Set 2 self-corrections only, first try | 70% | 3% | 28% | - |
| All sets after tuning on them | 99-100% | 0% | 0-1% | 80/80 |

Reading: rules reach the bar only after seeing the data, so the honest state is 88% exact, 3% wrong. The 80% self-correction bar was missed on the first try (70%). Wrong answers came from three causes, all now fixed and all worth keeping as rules: a follow-up after a handed-off turn, a question with no money verb about an account ("how much is in Revolut" is a balance), and words that are both a verb and a correction ("make that"). A new blind set is needed before quoting a final number, and the learned tagger (later step) has to beat 88/3.

Early cards: in 49-60% of partial transcripts the card is complete but not yet the final one ("how much did I spend" before "on groceries"). So nothing may be spoken the moment a card looks complete; the gate (pause detection) and number-last speech are required, not optional. True wrong-number exposure needs word timings from audio and is not measured yet.

Speed: one edit 0.1 ms. Whole fast path (edit + query + sentence) on a synthetic ledger: 2,000 rows 4 ms median / 9 ms p95; 20,000 rows 33 / 95 ms; 100,000 rows 176 / 505 ms. `investigate()` fingerprints every row it is given (sort + SHA-256), which cost 225 ms at 20,000 rows until the fast path pre-filtered rows by date.

Not covered yet, by design (all go to the chat model): balances, net worth, budgets, recurring, forecasts, averages, exclusions, amount conditions, single transactions, tags, synonyms ("food" for Groceries), every write.

## 9. Plan after the audit

See `plan.html` (rebuilt) for the diagrams. Order:

| Step | Build | Gate (loop until it passes) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Card, editor rules, speech, fast answer (done) | E4: 80%+ exact on a fresh blind set, 2% or less wrong, 100% of out-of-scope refused |
| 2 | Fast path inside today's GPT-Live call, text only: answered turns skip `/api/chat`, are saved to the conversation, and fall back on null | E1 coverage on the owner's history; same answer as the agent 98%+; p95 under 150 ms |
| 3 | More card kinds: balances, net worth, recurring, budget left | E1 again: coverage up, wrong answers still 2% or less |
| 4 | Real-microphone harness on `moneo-qa` and the ears (echo cancelling + a model that also hears the playback) | E2 |
| 5 | Local engine behind a setting: Whistle + turn head in, Pocket TTS / Woof out, same event names as today | First sound under 500 ms median; numbers spoken right 99%+ |
| 6 | Re-bindable speech and the number guard (digit sequence of what was synthesised vs the card) | E3; wrong number reaching the speaker under 1% |
| 7 | Learned editor: distil a small tagger from the rules plus chat-model labels; rules stay as the safety net | Beats rules on a fresh blind set |
| 8 | Scoring: GPT-Live measured on the same script, FDB-v3 self-correction, EchoChain, Duplex Cue; write-up | Better than GPT-Live on self-correction and wrong-number rate |

content.text:
Step 1 is built and passes its checks; the audit, the new plan and the test loop are done. Step 2 has not started.

## What the audit said
"Right direction, wrong plan as written." Moneo already has the query language (`investigate()`), so I reuse it instead of inventing one. Several "nobody did this" claims were wrong and are corrected in the log. One claim survives, and that is what a thesis would rest on: a full-duplex call whose state is a real, runnable finance query that updates on every word.

## What exists now
- **Question card and editor:** every new word re-edits the card; the last correction wins; short follow-ups edit the previous card.
- **Safety check:** if any word is unexplained, the turn goes to the chat model.
- **Speech:** exact money in words, never rounded, with the number last.
- **Fast answer:** words → card → Moneo's own maths → sentence. It takes about 33 ms on a 20,000-row fake ledger, and it only reads, never writes.

The full suite (1,608 tests), lint and typecheck pass. Nothing is committed.

## Results
- **First-try score:** on 200 hand-written cases the code had never seen, it got 88% right, 3% wrong and handed 10% to the chat model. All 40 out-of-scope questions were refused.
- **Self-corrections:** 70% on first try, below the 80% bar.
- **After tuning:** 99–100% on all sets, but those sets are now used up. A fresh blind set is needed before quoting a final number.
- **Early cards:** about half of the half-finished sentences already look like a complete question. So the call must wait for a pause before speaking a number.

Everything is in [LOG.md](C:\Users\mgsuk\.t3\worktrees\Moneo\t3-846dd64c-f0b28664becb1320\research\voice-duplex\LOG.md) (sections 7–9) and [plan.html](C:\Users\mgsuk\.t3\worktrees\Moneo\t3-846dd64c-f0b28664becb1320\research\voice-duplex\plan.html).

## One decision for you
The coverage test tells us how many of your real past questions the fast path would answer. It is the gate for step 2 and decides which card kinds to add next. The script is ready ([coverage.mts](C:\Users\mgsuk\.t3\worktrees\Moneo\t3-846dd64c-f0b28664becb1320\research\voice-duplex\experiments\expE\coverage.mts)): it only reads and prints counts. I have only run it on the empty test backend, so it is unproven on real data.

The project rules forbid me from touching your own data without a yes. May I run it on your real Moneo data, or do you want to run it yourself?

Next is step 2: wiring the fast path into today's call, text only, with GPT-Live still speaking.

  (ChatGPT sign-in, bank certificate), `backups/`, `logs/`, `chromium/` (the window's own cookies).

address and ChatGPT's callback name it). If it is taken on the first run, a free port is saved instead.

  then the app window opens Home. On failure it offers Try again, Open logs folder, Restore from backup, Quit.

  Quit (tray, Cmd+Q, `Moneo --quit`, OS shutdown) stops the server, then the database, then exits.
- Daily automatic backup while running; Back up now, Open backups folder and Restore from backup in the tray.
- Sign-ins (ChatGPT, banks, Scalable) open in the system browser and return to Moneo's loopback
  callbacks. The callback then opens its result (Import or Settings) in the app window and brings it

## 10. Step 2: fast path inside today's call (2026-11-15)

E1 on real history could not run. The owner said yes, but there is nothing to mine on this laptop: the desktop app's database is new (0 questions, 0 transactions, 12 default categories) and no older `moneo` database or volume exists. `coverage.mts` / `coverage_desktop.mts` are ready (read-only transaction, counts only) and ran clean on both the test backend and the desktop database. Coverage will instead collect from real calls: every turn code answers is saved with the tool name `voice_fast_answer`, so the same script can count them later.

Built:

| Where | Change |
|---|---|
| `lib/ai/voice-fast-path.ts` | `voiceFastPath()`: owned names + last card -> `editCard` -> `runInvestigation` (the same function as the chat tool `finance_investigate`) -> one sentence with digits. The card coming back from the browser is dropped unless every name on it is still the owner's |
| `app/api/chat/route.ts` | A call turn tries the fast path first, under the same data-scope checks as the tools (`accounts` + `transactions`). Null or any error: the model runs as before. Skipped while another request of the call is still running |
| `lib/ai/voice-call-controller.ts` | Keeps the card between turns; sends it only when nothing else is running; forgets it after a turn the model answered |
| `lib/ai/voice-call.ts` | The call brief may carry `card`; it is stripped from replayed history like the rest of the brief |

Checked through the real route on the test backend (`qa_server_3101.mjs` + `call_turns_qa.mjs`, dev server, empty workspace, placeholder AI key):

| Turn | Who answered | Time |
|---|---|---|
| "how much did I spend on groceries last month" | code | (first hit compiles) |
| "no wait, this month" | code, edited the card | 627 ms |
| "and compared to the month before?" | code | 484 ms |
| "how many transactions were there this year" | code, new card | 341 ms |
| "what is my net worth" | handed to the model (fails there by design: placeholder key) | - |
| "and last year?" right after | handed to the model, not answered from the stale card | - |

These are dev-server times including sign-in, the request claim and the save; the model path measured 1.5-2.7 s to first token alone in section 2. Not yet measured: a production build, a workspace with real rows, and a real call with GPT-Live speaking the result.

Open before this could merge to main: whether the fast path should sit behind a Labs setting (it replaces the model's wording with one fixed sentence on covered turns), and a link to the investigation page in the saved answer.

content.thinking:
I'm going through the 19 clips, 18 of them real, and noticing that most requests are writes: adding spending entries, an Amazon top-up, a subscription going up in price, a train ticket, and a salary figure. Roughly eight of the eighteen are like that, and the rest are reads about monthly and last-month spending.

Checking the read-only cases against the audit gate, I'm counting only about four or five of the eighteen real clips. That's roughly 22–28%, below the 35% threshold. The self-corrections I'm seeing ("not Rewe, it was Lidl", "not ten euros, twenty") all come from writes, which suggests the editable draft card idea should extend to proposal cards too.

Now I'm looking at how Whistle handles this real voice: "Rewe" comes out as "ravage," "Lidl" as "little," and "Spotify subscription" as "the strategy of subscription," with "how much did I spend" even turning into "how Mr. Desmond." Latency is 1.3–3.5 seconds on clips averaging around 8 seconds, far from the short synthetic samples I measured earlier. So the speech recognition is the weak link here, and I'd want a stronger local model like faster-whisper as a reference point.

I'm going to run a stronger reference speech model, faster-whisper large-v3-turbo on CPU, to get a pseudo ground-truth transcript. Then I can measure how far Whistle's output drifts and decide whether to fine-tune it or swap the recognizer.

I'm going to test the fast path against the real recordings, with the reference transcripts and seeded names like Rewe, Lidl, and Amazon. The main thing I want to check is whether it wrongly answers anything, since a simple question like "how much did I spend this month" could get cut down to leftover words and handed off.

Your recording gave 18 real questions; a first look shows many of your requests are "add this" and the small speech model mishears a lot. I'm getting a stronger reference transcript to measure that properly.

## 13. First real recording from the owner (2026-11-16)

One 251 s phone recording with 18 spoken requests, said the way the owner really talks. Audio and transcripts stay outside the repo (`<home>/moneo-voice-tests/call1`); only the scripts are here (`experiments/expF`, `experiments/expE/real_call.ts`). Split at pauses of 1 s with Silero VAD, transcribed with Whistle and, as a reference, Whisper large-v3-turbo (no human transcript exists, so "difference" below is against that reference, which favours Whisper-family models).

What the owner actually asks (18 requests):

| Kind | Count | Examples (paraphrased) |
|---|---|---|
| Add something | 8 (44%) | "I spent five euros at Rewe for groceries, add that", a subscription, a train ticket, cash in the wallet, a salary |
| Read a number | 5 (28%) | spending this month, last month, earnings from salary this year, groceries for the whole year |
| What-if, advice, other tools | 5 (28%) | change jobs, cancel one subscription for another, "is this above my median", check the broker |

Findings:

1. **Coverage on first contact was 0 of 18**, even with the reference transcript, against 99% on the generated test sets. Nothing was answered wrongly; every turn was handed to the chat model. The generated sets were too clean: real requests are long (mean 8 s, up to 18 s), start with a greeting or context, and use "can you check / find out / I wanted to ask".
2. **Every self-correction in the recording (4 of 4) was inside an "add" request**: the shop ("not Rewe, Lidl"), the amount twice ("not ten, twenty", then in a new turn "not even twenty, twenty-four"), and an estimate replaced by the real price. The question card cannot hold any of these. The thing people correct mid-sentence is the draft of a new record, not the query.
3. **A wrong answer the generated sets never produced**: after "earnings from salary this year", the whole question "can you check how my groceries are for the whole year" was treated as an edit of the previous card and became "income, Groceries". Fixed: a whole question without a money verb starts a new card. Also fixed: "this month and also last month" is two questions and goes to the chat model; "the whole year" is a period; "wanted, ask, check, find, exactly" are harmless words.
4. After these fixes code answers 4 of 18 with the reference transcript (3 of 18 with Whistle), 0 wrong. That is 4 of the 5 read requests; the fifth asks for three periods at once.
5. **Whistle on this voice**: 19% of words differ from the reference and only 75% of the key words survive (shop names, "euros", "add", "spend", "earn"). Examples: "Rewe" heard as "ravage", "euros" as "years", "add that" as "had that", "how much did I spend" as a person's name, "earn" as "own". Time is 18-20% of the clip length (1.3-3.5 s for 8-18 s clips, not streaming).

| Recogniser | Words that differ | Key words kept | Time vs audio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Whistle (17 MB) | 19% | 75% | 20% |
| Whisper tiny.en | 17% | 82% | 15% |
| Whisper base.en | 11% | 90% | 18% |
| Whisper small.en | 7% | 92% | 51% |
| Distil-Whisper small.en | 12% | 80% | 51% |

What this changes in the plan:

- Step 3 becomes **draft cards for adding things** (amount, shop, category, date, account), edited by speech the same way and shown as a card the owner taps. This is where the real corrections are, and it is 44% of requests. Balances and net worth move behind it.
- The recogniser has to be chosen on real recordings, not on synthetic speech. Whistle alone is not good enough for this voice today; options are a bigger small model (base.en is clearly better at the same speed), or adapting Whistle to the owner's voice and names.
- Real recordings are now the test set. Generated sets stay as a regression check only.

Your recording showed that the current build fits real calls badly: at first, code would have answered 0 of your 18 requests. Nothing was answered wrongly; every request went to the chat model. I split the file into 18 clips, transcribed them with Whistle and with a large reference model, and ran both through the editor.

| Kind | Count | Example |
|---|---|---|
| "Add this" | 8 | "I spent five euros at Rewe, add that" |
| "How much…" | 5 | spending this month, groceries for the whole year |
| What-if, advice, other | 5 | switching jobs, cancelling Netflix, checking Scalable |

## What I learned

- **My test sets were too clean.** They scored 99%; your real speech is longer, with greetings and "can you check…".
- **All four of your corrections were inside "add" requests** ("not Rewe, Lidl", "not ten, twenty", "not even 20, it's 24"). The card I built only handles "how much" questions, so it can't hold any of them.
- **Your recording exposed a wrong answer.** After a salary question, "how are my groceries this year" became "income for groceries". That is fixed, with a test.
- **After fixes, code answers 4 of 18** with a good transcript (3 with Whistle), 0 wrong. That is 4 of your 5 "how much" questions.
- **Whistle mishears your voice too often.** It heard "Rewe" as "ravage", "euros" as "years" and "add that" as "had that".

| Speech model | Words that differ from reference | Key words kept | Time vs audio |
|---|---|---|---|

- **Reading, about 3 minutes:** I send you about 30 sentences and you read them aloud. Then I know the exact words, so I can measure the speech models properly and train one on your voice.

# Reading script for voice tests

Thirty sentences with known words, so a recording of them can be scored exactly. Anyone can read it: every extra voice (accent, speed, microphone) makes the test set better.

How to record:

- One recording for all thirty, on a phone or laptop, in a normal room.
- Say the number of the sentence first is **not** needed. Just leave about two seconds of silence between sentences.
- Speak the way you normally would, not slowly or carefully. If you stumble, carry on; do not repeat.
- Save the file outside the repository (for the owner: `moneo-voice-tests/<your name>-reading.m4a`). Recordings are personal data and are never committed.

## Questions

1. How much did I spend this month?
2. How much did I spend on groceries last month?
3. What did I pay at Rewe in October?
4. How much did I earn from my salary this year?
5. Can you check how much I spent at Lidl this week?
6. How many times did I pay Netflix this year?
7. Did I spend more on restaurants this month than last month?
8. Where did my money go last month?
9. How much did I spend on Amazon in the last thirty days?
10. How much went on transport yesterday?

## Adding things

11. I spent five euros at Rewe for groceries, can you add that?
12. I just paid twelve euros fifty at Lidl, please add it.
13. Add a hundred euros for Amazon, I bought headphones.
14. I got my salary today, one thousand three hundred forty-three euros, add that.
15. I paid twenty-eight euros for a train ticket to Munich.
16. I spent one euro fifty on laundry just now.
17. Netto, seventeen euros, groceries, add it.
18. I pay twenty-four euros a month for ChatGPT, add that as a subscription.
19. I have seventeen euros in my wallet right now.
20. Yesterday I spent nine euros at Starbucks for coffee.

## Changing your mind

21. How much did I spend last month, no wait, this month?
22. I spent ten euros at Rewe, sorry, not Rewe, it was Lidl.
23. Add twenty euros for Spotify, no, it's not twenty, it's twenty-four.
24. What did I spend on groceries, I mean restaurants, in September?
25. I paid fifteen euros at Netto, actually make that fifty.

## Things only the chat assistant can answer

26. What is my net worth right now?
27. How much is in my N26 account?
28. Am I over budget this month?
29. If I cancel Netflix, how much do I save in a year?
30. Can you check Scalable and tell me how my stocks are doing?
